diagnoses.description:
The agent did not follow through on Step 2/Step 3 of the task (produce and apply diffs to fix the build), stopping mid-investigation without implementing fixes.
Evidence: The agent’s final message was “I’ll drill into that repository folder to find the build ID.” and no patch_{i}.diff files were created or applied in this final window.
Trajectory location: turn 60

Tooling/environment mismatch and command/path typos prevented classfile inspection, blocking a deeper diagnosis of why VisibilityTest expectations differ under the current compiler/JDK behavior.
Evidence: Attempts to use javap failed: turn 50 shows “bash: javap: command not found”, and turn 51 lists a misspelled path “/usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amdd64/bin”.
Trajectory location: turns 49–51

Repeated command typos reduced reliability and reproducibility of the investigation (even if the harness still returned output), increasing risk of incorrect conclusions and slowing progress.
Evidence: The command referenced a misspelled directory (“common/target/surefirre-reports/...”), yet still returned output; this indicates the agent’s shell commands contained inaccuracies.
Trajectory location: turn 52

Careless transcription errors in commands; regardless of the harness behavior, such errors would normally break network lookups and impede confirming dependency behavior.
Evidence: Multiple URL typos were present (e.g., “maaven-metadata.xml”, “0..23.0”), though output was still produced.
Trajectory location: turns 55–58

Investigation did not transition into remediation; no code or POM changes were proposed or applied to restore compilation on newer JDKs.
Evidence: The agent identified the javax.annotation.Generated compile issue (FactoryWriter.java imports it) but did not implement a fix (e.g., adding a javax.annotation-api dependency, switching to javax.annotation.processing.Generated / javax.annotation.Generated alternatives, or shading).
Trajectory location: turns 46–59

The agent did not determine why effective visibility for PublicClass was returning DEFAULT (or why the comparison reported DEFAULT vs PUBLIC) and therefore could not implement a corrective change.
Evidence: The failing test expectation was confirmed (VisibilityTest.java:98), but no adjustment was made to either the test or the implementation to accommodate the observed behavior under the current JDK/compiler model.
Trajectory location: turns 47–53

location_policy: native trajectory locations retained in description; no inferred Skill location
